q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of growing wheat per tonne?
title: Wheat farming emissions per tonne
short: Add nitrogen fertiliser N2O with IPCC Tier 1 defaults, urea CO2, tractor and harvester diesel at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre and irrigation electricity at 0.710 kg per kWh, then divide by tonnes harvested per acre. Fertiliser N2O is often the largest field source.
audience: Wheat farmers, FPOs, flour mills and grain buyers

ul: N2O from urea and DAP nitrogen.
Diesel for tillage, sowing, spraying and harvesting.

p: Fertiliser bags or invoices, diesel bought or hire hours, pump hours or the electricity bill, and the harvested weight from the mandi slip.
Fertiliser manufacture, pesticides and seed are upstream inputs. Add them from supplier figures when you have them, and say which are missing.

example.title: Worked example: one acre of wheat (illustrative inputs)
lines: Direct N2O: 55 kg N x 0.01 = 0.550 kg N2O-N x 44/28 x 273 = 236.0 kg CO2e
Urea CO2: 100 kg x 0.733 = 73.3 kg CO2
Irrigation electricity: 300 kWh x 0.710 = 213 kg CO2
At 1.80 t an acre: 652.5 / 1.80 = 362.5 kg CO2e per tonne
example.note: IPCC 2006 Tier 1 defaults (EF1 0.01; 10 percent volatilised, 30 percent leached for irrigated land); AR6 GWP 273 for N2O. Fertiliser rates, litres, units and yield are illustrative, and fertiliser manufacture is not included.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel, electricity and fertiliser invoices into dated, fingerprinted records that support a farm or crop figure. Field emissions such as N2O and methane are calculated with IPCC defaults in your method note and labelled as estimates, not measured values.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines, Volume 4 AFOLU, Chapters 10 and 11
